 TAMIL NADU PUBLIC HOLIDAY NOVEMBER 9 2026 
 Tamil Nadu Declares Public Holiday on November 9
 State authorities have declared an official holiday on November 9 (Monday) for schools, colleges, state PSUs, and government offices following Deepavali. While educational institutions and public offices remain closed, treasuries and sub-treasuries will operate with essential staff. November 28 will function as a compensatory working day.  Government of Tamil Nadu has officially declared November 9, 2026 (Monday), as a public holiday across the state for government offices, public sector undertakings (PSUs), schools, colleges, and other educational institutions. The announcement comes ahead of Deepavali, which falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026.
 The decision has been taken following requests from students, parents, teachers, and government employees who are planning to travel to their hometowns to celebrate the festival. The additional holiday will provide them with more time for travel and post-festival arrangements. However, November 28, 2026 (Saturday), will be observed as a regular working day to compensate for the additional holiday.
 Students and parents can also check the latest school holiday updates for October 2026 to stay informed about state-wise school closures and upcoming holidays.
 Tamil Nadu Holiday on November 9, 2026: Overview
 The Tamil Nadu government has announced an additional public holiday on November 9 following Deepavali celebrations. The holiday will apply to government departments, state public sector undertakings, schools, colleges, and other educational institutions across the state.

 Why Has Tamil Nadu Declared a Holiday on November 9?
 Deepavali, one of the major festivals celebrated across India, falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026. Since the festival coincides with a weekend, students, teachers, parents, and government employees requested an additional holiday on the following Monday.
 Several representations were made to the state government seeking an additional day to facilitate travel to native places and allow people to return after festival celebrations.
 Considering these requests, the Government of Tamil Nadu approved November 9 as an additional public holiday. The decision will provide a longer break for eligible institutions and employees while allowing people to manage their festival-related travel plans.
 Which Institutions Will Remain Closed on November 9?
 According to the government announcement, the additional holiday will apply across several categories of institutions in Tamil Nadu.
 The following institutions will observe the holiday on November 9, 2026:
 Government Offices: All applicable state government departments and offices will remain closed.
 Public Sector Undertakings: State public sector undertakings will observe the additional holiday.
 Schools: Government schools and other covered educational institutions will remain closed.
 Colleges: Colleges across the state will observe the declared holiday.
 Other Educational Institutions: The holiday will also apply to other educational institutions covered under the government order.
 Students appearing for upcoming board examinations should continue checking their respective academic schedules. They can also refer to the Tamil Nadu Board Exam Time Table 2027 for important examination dates and schedule-related updates.
 Treasury Operations and Compensatory Working Day
 Although November 9 has been declared a public holiday, certain essential government services will continue to operate.
 The government has clarified that the additional holiday will not fall under the provisions of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. Therefore, district collectors have been instructed to ensure that treasuries and sub-treasuries across Tamil Nadu remain operational with essential staff.
 This arrangement will help maintain important financial and administrative services and ensure that urgent government-related work is not disrupted.
 To compensate for the additional holiday, November 28, 2026 (Saturday), has been declared a regular working day for the affected government offices, public sector undertakings, schools, colleges, and other educational institutions.
 Important Updates for Students and Educational Institutions
 Students, parents, and teachers should take note of the revised holiday schedule and plan their travel and academic activities accordingly. Schools and colleges should also follow the instructions issued by the state government regarding the additional holiday and compensatory working day.
 Teachers and candidates preparing for eligibility examinations can also check the TNTET Notification 2026 for the latest examination and application updates.
 For students following other board examination schedules, the CBSE Class 12 Date Sheet 2027 page provides the latest timetable-related information.
 Tamil Nadu Public Holiday FAQs
 Why was a public holiday declared on November 9 in Tamil Nadu?
 The holiday was granted to accommodate travel plans for students, parents, teachers, and government employees returning from their hometowns after Deepavali celebrations on November 8. Which institutions remain closed on November 9?
 All state government offices, state public sector undertakings, schools, colleges, and educational institutions across Tamil Nadu will remain closed. Will treasuries and sub-treasuries remain open on November 9?
 Yes, district collectors have been directed to ensure that treasuries and sub-treasuries remain functional with essential staff to handle urgent administrative and financial tasks. Have questions about your prep?
